explanation: The hypothesis accurately reconstructs the central intervention: closed-loop high-throughput optimization of composition and continuous-solvothermal processing, with post-ageing performance as the design objective. It correctly identifies the 1 wt% La-doped alumina-supported catalyst space, severe 900 °C lean/rich wet ageing, multicomponent model exhaust, Pd/Al2O3 and random-search baselines, Cu–Pt electronic reconstruction, detrimental Pt–Ni/Fe interactions, and the specified performance thresholds. Conditions are slightly incomplete because pressure, reagent-flow variables, the full feed composition, 500 °C oxidation/reduction details, and heating rate are omitted. The proposed experiment is strongly discriminating for post-ageing activity and structural mediation, but it does not directly isolate H2O/NO poisoning resistance, quantify lifetime durability beyond the accelerated protocol, or reproduce the predictive-versus-random statistical comparison. Evidence discipline is the main weakness: no prior evidence is actually cited, and the poison-resistance and Cu–Pt causal claims are somewhat stronger than the selected ex situ FT-IR/STEM evidence warrants. The disjunctive falsification rule is also imperfect because failure to observe Cu–Pt bands could reflect characterization sensitivity rather than failure of the activity hypothesis.
